newsitem.title: UK: Euro stocks end with big gains after US data.
newsitem.headline: Euro stocks end with big gains after US data.

text.p: European stocks roared ahead to close with big gains on Tuesday, lifted by U.S. economic data which showed reduced inflationary pressures and helped calm interest rate worries.
Frankfurt and Paris climbed by two percent shortly after U.S. figures were released giving welcome figures on employment costs and durable goods. London was boosted by one percent.

Wall Street itself rapidly climbed 1.6 percent on the back of a powerful rally in the bond market after Washington reported the favourable statistics. The sudden surge activated the New York Stock Exchange's limits on program trading.
Feeding the bullish mood were the data on lower-than-expected labour costs and an unanticipated drop of 3.0 percent in durable goods orders in March, the largest drop since August 1996.

Markets on both sides of the Atlantic saw the data as good news, suggesting the economy's growth may be slowing and inflation was still in check -- lessening the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again at its May 20 meeting.

On currency markets, the data had the opposite effect , hurting the dollar as the receding prospects of higher interest rates knocked the U.S. currency off its recent high levels agains the mark and yen.

French stocks were given the biggest lift by the data to close up 52.61 points, or 2.06 percent, at 2,602.86. The euphoria sparked by data offset worries over the upcoming French election which had been clouding sentiment.
"Fifty points is quite exceptional," said a broker. Volume though was moderate.
Index heavyweights to rise strongly included Alcatel
Alsthom, up 4.17 percent at 649, and Societe Generale up 4.52 percent at 648.
In Frankfurt, shares spurted ahead, following in the path of government bonds on the strength of the Washington figures.

Floor trade had ended before the Washington data, but transactions on the computerised IBIS index climbed 63.75 points to 3435.71 and breached a key resistance level at 3,400 points before slipping back slightly near the close..
"Things are certainly positive in the very short term but I wouldn't see this as real euphoria," cautioned one trader.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks jumped by one percent to close at its highest level for six weeks after a day of dull trading overshadowed by Thursday's British general election.

"We have seen quite an incredible performance recently considering the election is round the corner," said one dealer. "The financials have been largely responsible for driving us higher and most of today's gains came from the States and rethinking on interest rates," the dealer said.
On currency markets, the dollar weakened as the Washington figures dampened hopes of near-term rise in interest rates, which would hurt dollar-denominated assets.
"The data dented rate rise hopes, and that's pulling the dollar lower," said David Bloom at HSBC James Capel.
Near the close, the dollar, against the mark, dropped below the levels seen in late trading on Monday but was little changed gainst the yen.
But expectations of stronger first-quarter GDP figures on Wednesday and healthy jobs data on on Friday should help keep the dollar well supported, traders said.
"The dollar remains well supported by fundamentals, and until the picture of a robust U.S. economy remains intact, it's going to be well underpinned," said Bloom, a currency economist.
STOCKS CLOSING PRICES
London's FTSE 100 ended up 43.5 points at 4,433.2.
The Paris CAC-40 index finished up 52.61 points at 2602.86.
Frankfurt's DAX index closed up 20.13 at 3,383.19. The IBIS index ended up 52.90 points at 3425.86.
CURRENCIES AT 1615 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7235 marks versus 1.7274 in late European trade on Monday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.75 from 126.61.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $339.95 after ending at $340.05 in London on Monday. Silver was at $4.65, down a cent, in late trade.
